newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat crop seen crippled by record cold.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat crop seen crippled by record cold.

text.p: Record cold in Kansas over the weekend will cause serious damage to the wheat crop in the southern two-thirds of the state, an agronomist said.
"We had a good crop and basically the potential for a good crop is out the window. Right now it is pretty depressing," said Kansas State University wheat breeder Rollie Sears.

"You have basically killed most of your fall tillers (in southern Kansas)..in which case depending on how favorable the growing season is, you've got anywhere from 20 to 50 percent damage," Sears said, noting problems would be less severe in the northern third of the state where the crop hasn't jointed.
Sears estimated that 50 to 75 percent of fall tillers may have been lost in the southern two-thirds of the state.
He said spring tillers could now grow, but they on average yielded 40 percent less than fall tillers.
"If we've lost the majority of our fall tillers we are looking at about a 40 percent yield loss. Right now it really depends on what kind of spring we get," Sears said.
Crops north of I-70, representing about the northern third of the state, had generally not jointed, he said.
"Soil temperatures probably didn't get low enough to damage those plants," he said.
Saturday, temperatures dipped to five degrees Fahrenheit in Goodland, Kan., 10 degrees at Garden City, and 14 at Dodge City, meteorologists said.
"This is by far the worst cold we've seen in April ever. Out west it broke historical records by eight, nine, 10, 11 degrees," Sears said.
